revision_rule.note: The 2017 rule states that break jumps out of the loop; because a multidimensional foreach is one loop, this also exits the entire foreach.
The 2017 rule transfers to the loop end and executes loop control; for multidimensional foreach, the loop control advances after the current complete index tuple.
The 2012 rule permits foreach over array types but does not treat a scalar string as a dynamic byte array indexed from 0 through N-1.
The 2017 clause permits foreach over arrays but does not specify the 2023 treatment of a string variable as a dynamic byte array indexed 0 through N-1.
The 2012 standard has no foreach restriction forbidding a function call in the array-designating identifier as an implicit variable declaration.
The 2017 foreach grammar restricts the designator to ps_or_hierarchical_array_identifier, excluding a function call.
The 2012 pattern grammar has the identifier, wildcard, constant, tagged-member, and structure forms but does not include the 2023 parenthesized-pattern alternative.
The 2017 Syntax 12-4 has the identifier, wildcard, constant, tagged-member, and structure forms but does not include the 2023 parenthesized-pattern alternative.
The 2012 Syntax 12-1 additionally enumerates a standalone inc_or_dec_expression followed by a semicolon as a statement-item alternative.
The 2017 Syntax 12-1 additionally permits a standalone inc_or_dec_expression statement item, which is absent from the 2023 enumeration.

The 2017 clause says repeat executes a fixed number of times but does not provide the 2023 explicit guarantee that the count expression is evaluated once before the loop and unaffected by body changes.
The 2012 rule treats unknown and high-impedance repeat counts as zero but does not specify that a negative repeat count is treated as zero.
The 2017 clause treats X and Z repeat counts as zero but does not include the 2023 rule that a negative count is treated as zero.
